title: dump_now: take one live dump of the running game from a second terminal
summary: A dump is a snapshot of the game's memory ranges that the running script chose at start (player record, weapon set, inventory block and so on). It is written to a file next to the session folder and the game goes on, nothing in the game is changed. You run this helper in a SECOND terminal at the moment you want the snapshot, so the label names what was on the screen.
prerequisites: The game must already be running, started by one of the dump scripts (run_weaponslot_probe, run_weaponslot_session, run_inventory_session, run_button_dumps, run_forced_weapons). The helper finds the newest session under tmp/owner-profiles whose host process is still alive.
Open a second terminal in the repo root. Do not run it in the terminal of the session script.

steps.text: Get the game into the state you want to capture and stand still (for example in the Map Maker preview with the weapon placed, or just after leaving the preview).
substeps: Take the dump while that state is on screen, not later.

steps.text: In the second terminal run: fish tmp/dump_now.fish {label}
substeps: Without a label the name is 'preview'. A label may contain lowercase letters, digits, underscore and dash and nothing else. Use a new label each time, a second dump with the same label most likely replaces the first (INFERRED, not tried).
Good labels say what you see: preview, left, after_pickup, editor_slot2.

steps.text: Read the answer. 'dump taken: DIR/guestdump.LABEL' is success and the file is there. 'no ack yet' means the game did not answer within 5 s (it may be busy): wait a few seconds, look whether the file DIR/guestdump.LABEL exists, and run it again if not.

note_at_end: What you were doing when you took each label, as one short line per label.
stop: Nothing to stop, the command ends by itself after a few seconds.
send_back: The printed line ('dump taken: ...' or 'no ack yet ...') and the folder name.
Per label, what was on the screen (the file name only carries the label).
